# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-03**
**Member:** Jordan Hayes
**Member ID:** W671447302
**Reference Number:** POC-92D596C7F2-83353
**Plan:** MedStar Family Choice DC (Commercial/ACA)
**Requested Service:** Lower back disc surgery / decompression, CPT 63030
**Governing Policy:** Utilization Management Criteria — https://www.medstarfamilychoicedc.com/-/media/project/mho/mfcdc/medical-policies-and-procedures/policy-115dc_utilization-management-criteria.pdf

Dear Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of my request for lower back disc surgery / decompression (CPT 63030). My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking MedStar Family Choice DC to reconsider this decision.

## Why I believe the denial should be reversed

My denial notice states that this request was denied because "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I do not believe that is an accurate description of the record my surgeon submitted. The prior authorization packet includes the following, all documented in my chart:

- **18 months** of progressive lower back pain that has not improved with rest.
- **Completed conservative care**: 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (16 visits, 2026-04-14 through 2026-06-09), documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial**: 8 months of NSAIDs with inadequate relief, and a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-29 that gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging**: an MRI of the lumbar spine on 2026-06-16 showing an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root.
- **Functional limitation**: I cannot stand for more than 10 minutes, and I have radicular pain radiating into my right calf.
- **Physical exam findings**: positive provocative testing on the affected side and a neurologic deficit that corresponds to the level shown on my MRI.
- No active infection and no untreated substance use are noted in my record.

This is a substantial clinical record covering symptom duration, a completed course of conservative treatment, imaging, and a physical exam consistent with the imaging findings. If any specific piece of documentation is still considered missing, I am asking the plan to identify exactly what that is, so my surgeon's office can supply it.

## The plan's own policy on its criteria

The plan's Utilization Management Criteria policy states that "MedStar Family Choice DC follows documented UM criteria to facilitate consistency in UM decision making across all service types," and that "All criteria utilized in utilization management are available upon request." The policy also states: "The following criteria and processes, as documented on MedStar Family Choice DC web site, are utilized for UM decision making."

My denial notice does not identify which specific clinical criteria were applied to my request, or which piece of documentation was found incomplete. Without that information, I am not able to see how the records I submitted were measured against the plan's own standard.

## Request for the specific criteria applied

I understand that MedStar Family Choice DC may use InterQual criteria, which is licensed software and not something I can look up on my own. I am nonetheless entitled to it: under ERISA and ACA appeal rules, the plan must provide me, free of charge, with the specific rule or criterion relied on in my denial. I am formally requesting, in writing, **the InterQual subset, edition, and full criteria text applied to my determination** for CPT 63030, along with a clear statement of what documentation the plan considers missing from my file.

## What I am asking for

1. Please reconsider this denial in light of the clinical documentation summarized above.
2. Please provide, in writing, the specific criteria and any InterQual subset/edition applied to this determination.
3. Please identify, specifically, what documentation the plan considers incomplete, so my surgeon's office can supply it if it is missing from your records.

I understand my appeal must be received by **2027-01-30**. Please send your response, and direct this appeal, to the appeal address printed on my denial letter; if I cannot locate that address, I will call the number on the back of my insurance card to confirm where member appeals are filed.

Thank you for reviewing this appeal. I am relying on my surgeon's clinical judgment that this surgery is medically necessary, and I ask that the plan's review take into account the full record described above.

Sincerely,

______________________________
Jordan Hayes
Member ID: W671447302
Date: [date of signature]
Phone: [phone number]
Email: [email address]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*
